transcript.text: I can help you track that down. To start, does the vacuum make any noise at all when you try to use it, or is it completely silent? If it's silent, please check that the plug is firmly in the wall socket and that the main on/off switch (usually near the cord handle) is switched on.
its completely silent. plug is in and the switch clicks. it cut out when i was doing the stairs and wont come back on

Since it cut out while in use and is now completely silent, it has likely tripped a safety thermal cut-out due to overheating or a blockage. If it's cordless, the battery may have also failed or gone into deep protection mode. To help me guide you correctly: is your vacuum corded or cordless? If cordless, please check the model number (usually on a label under the bin or near the battery) and tell me what it says. If it's corded, could you please unplug it, leave it to cool for 30 minutes, then check the hose and floorhead for any blockages?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its corded, the red Henry one. i cant read the label, cant turn it over with my back. theres some black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago

That sounds like the thermal cut-out has tripped from overheating or a blockage while you were cleaning the stairs. Since you can't turn it over to check the model label right now, let's focus on the safety checks. 1. Unplug the vacuum and leave it to cool for 30 minutes.
2. While it cools, please check if there is a blockage in the hose or floorhead (you can shine a torch down them).
3. After 30 minutes, plug it back in and try turning it on. Also, regarding that black tape near the plug: once you have sorted the immediate issue, please inspect the cable carefully for any cuts or exposed wires under there. If the cable is damaged at all, do not use it until a qualified person replaces the plug or cable.
ok i can unplug it and wait. i havent got a torch though. it flickered on once when i moved the cable, is that important?

Yes, that is very important. If the vacuum flickers on only when you move the cable, it almost probably means there is a broken wire inside the cord. The movement makes contact briefly, but the connection isn't reliable. Because this involves mains electricity and a damaged power supply, please do not try to repair the cable yourself or use it further. You need to have the plug replaced or the entire cable swapped by a qualified electrician or appliance repair technician.

candidates: Power supply or switch issue (cord, plug, on/off switch) (high)
Clogged filter or blocked hose reducing suction to a stop (medium)
Overheating thermal cut-out (if it ran then died) (low)
